title: HMAC accumulation buffer: grow-by-doubling does not cap at WOLFSSL_CRYPTO2DEV_HMAC_MAX_BUF
description: In crypto2dev_hmac() Update path: new_cap doubles from dataCap, but is then bounded below by 'need' if need > new_cap. The cap bound (WOLFSSL_CRYPTO2DEV_HMAC_MAX_BUF) is checked against 'need' before allocation, rejecting inputs that would exceed it. But: if dataCap is 32 KB and the doubling produces 64 KB, and WOLFSSL_CRYPTO2DEV_HMAC_MAX_BUF is 64 KB, then new_cap (64 KB) equals the limit but need might be < 64 KB — so XMALLOC(64 KB) is called even though the actual data is smaller. This means XMALLOC can allocate up to new_cap = 2 * WOLFSSL_CRYPTO2DEV_HMAC_MAX_BUF - 1 bytes in the worst case (when dataCap is HMAC_MAX_BUF/2 and a single update fills exactly to HMAC_MAX_BUF). Not a correctness bug because the check 'need > WOLFSSL_CRYPTO2DEV_HMAC_MAX_BUF' fires before allocation. But a maintainer who changes HMAC_MAX_BUF without understanding the doubling strategy may inadvertently allow 2x the intended allocation.
